2608.22797.title: Performance of a domain-specific large language model in answering patient questions in psychiatry
2608.22797.paper_summary: Background This study was designed to evaluate whether a domain-specific large language model (LLM) trained exclusively on patient education resources can answer questions about psychiatric medications, in a manner superior to LLM chatbots. We developed an LLM ("MIND") fine-tuned for clinical fidelity, trained on patient education resources from authoritative medical organizations. Methods We compared the responses of MIND, ChatGPT, and OpenEvidence to patient questions about escitalopram, using two methods: (1) computer analysis according to a rubric measuring accuracy, clarity, completeness, nuance, safety, and referral appropriateness; (2) ratings from N=10 board-licensed psychiatrists on similar metrics. Results When rated by rubric, MIND was rated highest in all domains (p<0.001). When rated by psychiatrists, ChatGPT was rated accurate more often than MIND with a negligible effect size (p=0.021, r=0.073); MIND was rated complete more often than ChatGPT with a small effect size (p<0.001, r=0.160); and MIND and ChatGPT were rated safe with the same frequency (p=0.955, r=0.002). The majority of psychiatrists preferred the responses generated by ChatGPT (57.6%) compared to MIND (42.4%, p=0.003). Conclusions MIND was able to answer many questions about escitalopram in a manner deemed accurate, complete, and safe by psychiatrists the majority of the time. However, despite MIND's ability to provide more complete responses, psychiatrists preferred ChatGPT's responses. MIND represents a step towards building safe LLM systems to enhance patient education in psychiatry.
2608.22797.paper_summary_zh: 背景 本研究旨在評估一個專門針對患者教育資源訓練的大型語言模型（LLM）是否能以優於LLM聊天機器人的方式回答有關精神科藥物的問題。我們開發了一個名為“MIND”的LLM，專注於臨床準確性，並基於權威醫療機構的患者教育資源進行微調。<lb/>方法 我們比較了MIND、ChatGPT和OpenEvidence對患者有關艾司西酞普蘭的問題的回答，使用了兩種方法：（1）根據一個衡量準確性、清晰度、完整性、細緻度、安全性和轉診適當性的標準進行計算機分析；（2）由N=10名持牌精神科醫師對類似指標進行評分。<lb/>結果 根據標準評分，MIND在所有領域的評分最高（p<0.001）。在精神科醫師評分中，ChatGPT被評為準確的次數多於MIND，但效果大小微不足道（p=0.021，r=0.073）；MIND被評為完整的次數多於ChatGPT，效果大小較小（p<0.001，r=0.160）；MIND和ChatGPT的安全性評分頻率相同（p=0.955，r=0.002）。大多數精神科醫師偏好ChatGPT生成的回答（57.6%），而非MIND（42.4%，p=0.003）。<lb/>結論 MIND能夠以大多數精神科醫師認為準確、完整且安全的方式回答許多有關艾司西酞普蘭的問題。然而，儘管MIND能提供更完整的回答，精神科醫師仍偏好ChatGPT的回答。MIND代表了朝著建立安全的LLM系統以增強精神科患者教育邁出的一步。
